<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December 31, 2019, all of the available-for-sale securities have contractual maturities within <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000404" name="aimt:AvailableForSaleSecuritiesMaturitiesPeriod" contextRef="C_0001631650_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">two years</ix:nonNumeric>. We periodically review our available-for-sale investments for other-than-temporary impairment loss. We consider factors such as the duration, severity and the reason for the decline in value, the potential recovery period and our intent to sell. For debt securities, we also consider whether (i) it is more likely than not that we will be required to sell the debt securities before recovery of their amortized cost basis, and (ii) the amortized cost basis cannot be recovered as a result of credit losses. During the years ended December 31, 2019, 2018, and 2017 we did <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000405" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfInvestments" contextRef="C_0001631650_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000406" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfInvestments" contextRef="C_0001631650_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000407" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfInvestments" contextRef="C_0001631650_20170101_20171231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>t recognize any other-than-temporary impairment losses. All marketable securities with unrealized losses have been in a loss position for less than <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000408" name="aimt:MarketableSecuritiesUnrealizedLossesPositionMaximumPeriod" contextRef="C_0001631650_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">twelve months</ix:nonNumeric>. </p>

<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">5. Long-Term Debt, Net of Discounts </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In January 2019, we&#160;entered into a loan agreement with an affiliate of KKR for up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000441" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_20190131" decimals="INF" scale="6">170.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in&#160;<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_aimtTranche" id="F_000442" name="aimt:DebtInstrumentNumberOfTranches" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_20190131" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">three</ix:nonFraction>&#160;tranches, or the KKR Loans. Of the total loan amount, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000443" name="aimt:LineOfCreditFacilityProceedsReceivableUponClosingOfTransaction" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_20190131" decimals="-5" scale="6">40.0</ix:nonFraction> million was funded upon the closing of the transaction in January 2019 and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000444" name="aimt:LineOfCreditFacilityProceedsReceivableUponFDAApproval" contextRef="C_0001631650_srtStatementScenarioAxis_srtScenarioForecastMember_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_20200229" decimals="-5" scale="6">85.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million was funded in February 2020 following FDA approval of PALFORZIA and satisfaction of other customary borrowing conditions. The remaining $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000445" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityRemainingBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_20190131" decimals="-5" scale="6">45.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million is to be made available at our option in 2020, upon the satisfaction of certain borrowing conditions, including our achievement of aggregate net sales (as defined in the agreement) for PALFORIZA by July 31, 2020 in an amount of at least $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000446" name="aimt:AchievementOfAggerateNetSales" contextRef="C_0001631650_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_srtStatementScenarioAxis_srtScenarioForecastMember_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_20200731_20200731" decimals="INF" scale="6">30.0</ix:nonFraction> million. The KKR Loans have a maturity date being the earliest of (a)&#160;<ix:nonNumeric id="F_000447" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityExpirationDate1" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_20190130_20190131" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">January 3, 2025</ix:nonNumeric>, or if Regulatory Approval has not occurred on or before&#160;<ix:nonNumeric id="F_000448" name="aimt:RegulatoryApprovalLastDate" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_20190130_20190131" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">December 31, 2020</ix:nonNumeric>,&#160;<ix:nonNumeric id="F_000449" name="aimt:LineOfCreditFacilityWithoutRegulatoryApprovalExpirationDate" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_20190130_20190131" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">January 15, 2021</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;and (b) the date that is 91 days prior to the earliest current maturity date of any other loans we might have in excess of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000450" name="aimt:OtherLoansTriggerAmountToReduceMaturityOfCreditFacility" contextRef="C_0001631650_srtStatementScenarioAxis_srtScenarioForecastMember_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="6">15.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million prior to the funding of the third tranche of the KKR Loans or $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000451" name="aimt:OtherLoansTriggerAmountToReduceMaturityOfCreditFacility" contextRef="C_0001631650_srtStatementScenarioAxis_srtScenarioForecastMember_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_20210101" decimals="INF" scale="6">25.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million following the funding of the third tranche of the KKR Loans. The KKR Loans bear interest through maturity, at our election with respect to (a) Alternate Base Rate, or ABR Loans, ABR plus&#160;<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000452" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_us-gaapVariableRateAxis_us-gaapBaseRateMember_20190130_20190131" decimals="INF" scale="-2">6.50</ix:nonFraction>% per annum and (b) London Interbank Offered Rate, or LIBOR Loans, 30-day LIBOR plus&#160;<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000453" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_us-gaapVariableRateAxis_us-gaapLondonInterbankOfferedRateLIBORMember_20190130_20190131" decimals="INF" scale="-2">7.50</ix:nonFraction>% per annum. We have the option to elect to make interest payments from available funds or make interest payments in kind by capitalizing such interest amounts on the applicable interest payment date by adding the amounts to the outstanding principal amount of the loan. Any capitalized amounts also bear interest.&#160;To date, we have selected to pay in kind and capitalized the interest for the year ending December 31, 2019. We began accruing interest on the outstanding KKR Loans on March 31, 2019, and continue to accrue interest on the outstanding KKR loans on the last business day of each March, June, September and December thereafter while any KKR Loan is outstanding, as well as on the final maturity date of the KKR Loans, with each such date being referred to herein as an Interest Payment Date.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Principal payments on the KKR Loans are paid according to the following schedule: (i) on December 31, 2023,&#160;<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000454" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentRedemptionPricePercentage" contextRef="C_0001631650_srtStatementScenarioAxis_srtScenarioForecastMember_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_20231231_20231231" decimals="3" scale="-2">50.0</ix:nonFraction>% of the outstanding principal amount of the loans as of such date, including any capitalized interest, (ii) on each Interest Payment Date thereafter,&#160;<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000455" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityInterestRateDuringPeriod" contextRef="C_0001631650_srtStatementScenarioAxis_srtScenarioForecastMember_us-gaapLineOfCreditFacilityAxis_aimtKKRLoansMember_20231231_20231231" decimals="3" scale="-2">12.5</ix:nonFraction>% of the outstanding principal amount of the KKR Loans as of December 31, 2023 and (iii) on January 3, 2025, or the Maturity Date, any remaining outstanding balance of the KKR Loans. We are also required to make mandatory prepayments of the KKR Loans under the Agreement, subject to specified exceptions, with the proceeds of asset sales, debt issuances, royalty transactions, collaboration transactions, and specified other events. In addition, upon the occurrence of a change of control, we must prepay, the outstanding amount of the KKR Loans.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000265" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001631650_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000265_dcnt_00f46e02-2713-43a5-bb1c-18a37e619a9d">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">6. Commitments and Contingencies</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Leases</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Facility Leases</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000475" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseDescription" contextRef="C_0001631650_20190101_20191231"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000476" name="us-gaap:LesseeFinanceLeaseDescription" contextRef="C_0001631650_20190101_20191231">We lease facilities for&#160;office and manufacturing space under various operating leases and a security system under a financing lease.</ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric>&#160;<ix:nonNumeric id="F_000480" name="us-gaap:LesseeFinanceLeaseOptionToExtend" contextRef="C_0001631650_20190101_20191231"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000478" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseOptionToExtend" contextRef="C_0001631650_20190101_20191231">Our leases have remaining lease terms of approximately&#160;<ix:nonNumeric id="F_000473" name="aimt:LesseeOperatingAndFinanceLeasesRemainingLeaseTerm" contextRef="C_0001631650_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">1</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;year to&#160;<ix:nonNumeric id="F_000474" name="aimt:LesseeOperatingAndFinanceLeasesRemainingLeaseTerm" contextRef="C_0001631650_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">6</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;years, which represent the non-cancellable periods of the leases and include extension options that we determined are reasonably certain to be exercised. We exclude extension options that are not reasonably certain to be exercised from our lease terms.</ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric>&#160;Our lease payments consist primarily of fixed rental payments for the right to use the underlying leased assets over the lease terms. We often receive customary incentives from our landlords, such as reimbursements for tenant improvements and rent abatement periods, which effectively reduce the total lease payments owed for these leases.</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#212529;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Operating lease right-of-use assets and liabilities on our consolidated balance sheets represent the present value of our remaining lease payments over the remaining lease terms. We do not allocate lease payments to non-lease components.&#160;<ix:nonNumeric id="F_000481" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseVariableLeasePaymentTermsAndConditions" contextRef="C_0001631650_20190101_20191231"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000482" name="us-gaap:LesseeFinanceLeaseVariableLeasePaymentTermsAndConditions" contextRef="C_0001631650_20190101_20191231">We use our incremental borrowing rate to calculate the present value of our lease payments, as the implicit rates in our leases are not readily determinable.</ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In 2015, we entered into lease agreements for our corporate headquarters in Brisbane, California for <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_utrsqft" id="F_000483" name="us-gaap:AreaOfRealEstateProperty" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapMajorPropertyClassAxis_aimtHeadquartersMember_us-gaapOtherCommitmentsAxis_aimtFacilityLeasesMember_20151231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">38,000</ix:nonFraction> square feet of office space, which was subsequently amended resulting in a total of approximately <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_utrsqft" id="F_000484" name="us-gaap:AreaOfRealEstateProperty" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapMajorPropertyClassAxis_aimtHeadquartersMember_us-gaapOtherCommitmentsAxis_aimtFacilityLeasesMember_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">58,000</ix:nonFraction> square feet of office space being leased. The term for the entire office space&#160;terminates on <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000485" name="us-gaap:LeaseExpirationDate1" contextRef="C_0001631650_20190101_20191231" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">June 30, 2024</ix:nonNumeric>. We are responsible for operating expenses over base operating expenses as defined in the original lease agreement. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June 2015, we signed a facility lease for a manufacturing facility in Clearwater, Florida for approximately <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_utrsqft" id="F_000486" name="us-gaap:AreaOfRealEstateProperty" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapMajorPropertyClassAxis_us-gaapManufacturingFacilityMember_us-gaapOtherCommitmentsAxis_aimtFacilityLeasesMember_20150630" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">20,000</ix:nonFraction> square feet of manufacturing space, which was subsequently amended resulting in a total of approximately <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_utrsqft" id="F_000487" name="us-gaap:AreaOfRealEstateProperty" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapMajorPropertyClassAxis_us-gaapManufacturingFacilityMember_us-gaapOtherCommitmentsAxis_aimtFacilityLeasesMember_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">30,000</ix:nonFraction> square feet of manufacturing space being leased. The lease is expected to expire in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000488">June 2025</span>.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In September 2018, we entered into a lease for office space in Durham, North Carolina for <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_utrsqft" id="F_000489" name="us-gaap:AreaOfRealEstateProperty" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapOtherCommitmentsAxis_aimtFacilityLeasesMember_20180930" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">5,099</ix:nonFraction> square feet of office space. The lease is expected to expire in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000490">February 2024</span>. </p>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In November 2018, we entered into a lease for part of a floor of office space in London, United Kingdom. <p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Asset Retirement Obligation</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We recognized the estimated fair value of our asset retirement obligation related to our office space in London, United Kingdom in long-term liabilities in November 2018. The fair value of the asset retirement obligation is also capitalized as construction in progress. The fair value of the asset retirement obligation was estimated by discounting projected cash flows over the estimated life of the related assets using our credit adjusted risk-free rate. Our asset retirement obligation consists of a contractual requirement to remove the tenant improvements at our office space in London, United Kingdom and restore the lease office space to a condition as specified in the lease agreement.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000302" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfAssetRetirementObligationsTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001631650_20190101_20191231" escape="true">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:3.33%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with our entry into the License Agreement, we also agreed to assume Xencor&#8217;s rights and obligations under its license of the AIMab7195 cell line from Catalent Pharma Solutions LLC, which manufactures AIMab7195 using their proprietary GPEx&#174; technology.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Indemnifications</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We indemnify each of our officers and directors for certain events or occurrences, subject to certain limits, while the officer or director is or was serving at our request in such capacity, as permitted under Delaware law and in accordance with its certificate of incorporation and bylaws. The term of the indemnification period lasts as long as an officer or a director may be subject to any proceeding arising out of acts or omissions of such officer or director in such capacity. The maximum amount of potential future indemnification is unlimited&#59; however, we currently hold director and officer liability insurance. This insurance allows the transfer of risk associated with our exposure and may enable us to recover a portion of any future amounts paid. We believe that the fair value of these indemnification obligations is minimal. Accordingly, we have not recognized any liabilities relating to these obligations for any period.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Legal</p>

<hr style="page-break-after:always" /><ix:continuation id="F_000268_dcnt_3377c298-9c5b-44c8-a4ab-b9915c0592ad" continuedAt="F_000268_dcnt_cf1c80e5-097e-47be-8ca3-b0318ccfa721">
<p style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We recognize deferred income taxes for temporary differences between the basis of assets and liabilities for financial statement and income tax purposes. We periodically evaluate the positive and negative evidence bearing upon realizability of our deferred tax assets. Based upon the weight of available evidence, which includes our historical operating performance, reported cumulative net losses since inception and difficulty in accurately forecasting our future results, we maintained a full valuation allowance on the net deferred tax assets as of December 31, 2019 and 2018.<span style="color:#000000;"> </span>We intend to maintain a full valuation allowance on the federal, foreign and state deferred tax assets until sufficient positive evidence exists to support reversal of the valuation allowance. The net change in the valuation allowance for the years ended December 31, 2019 and December 31, 2018 was an increase of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000810" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowanceDeferredTaxAssetChangeInAmount" contextRef="C_0001631650_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">79.3</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000811" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowanceDeferredTaxAssetChangeInAmount" contextRef="C_0001631650_20180101_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">41.6</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December 31, 2019, we had net operating loss, or NOL, carryforwards for Federal, California and other state income tax purposes of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000812" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">522.3</ix:nonFraction><span style="color:#auto;"> </span>million, $<span style="color:#auto;"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000813" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis_us-gaapCaliforniaFranchiseTaxBoardMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">12.0</ix:nonFraction></span> million, and $<span style="color:#auto;"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000814" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_aimtOtherStateJurisdictionMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">63.9</ix:nonFraction></span> million, respectively. As of December 31, 2018, we had NOL carryforwards for Federal, California and other state income tax purposes of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000815" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">326.4</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000816" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis_us-gaapCaliforniaFranchiseTaxBoardMember_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">12.0</ix:nonFraction> million, and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000817" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_aimtOtherStateJurisdictionMember_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">30.2</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, which will begin to expire in <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000818" name="aimt:NetOperatingLossCarryforwardExpirationYear" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20190101_20191231">2031</ix:nonNumeric>, <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000819" name="aimt:NetOperatingLossCarryforwardExpirationYear" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis_us-gaapCaliforniaFranchiseTaxBoardMember_20190101_20191231">2031</ix:nonNumeric>, and <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000820" name="aimt:NetOperatingLossCarryforwardExpirationYear" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_aimtOtherStateJurisdictionMember_20190101_20191231">2030</ix:nonNumeric>, respectively, if not utilized. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December 31, 2019, we had Federal and California research credit carryforwards of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000821" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationTaxCreditsResearch" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">17.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000822" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationTaxCreditsResearch" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis_us-gaapCaliforniaFranchiseTaxBoardMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">5.7</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. As of December 31, 2018, we had Federal and California research credit carryforward of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000823" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationTaxCreditsResearch" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">12.1</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000824" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationTaxCreditsResearch" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis_us-gaapCaliforniaFranchiseTaxBoardMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">3.1</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. The Federal research credits will begin to expire in <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000825" name="aimt:ResearchCreditCarryforwardExpirationYear" contextRef="C_0001631650_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20190101_20191231">2031</ix:nonNumeric>, while the California research credits have no expiration date.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Under Section&#160;382 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, or the Code, if a corporation undergoes an &#8220;ownership change,&#8221; generally defined as a greater than 50 percentage point change (by value) in its equity ownership over a rolling three-year period, the corporation&#8217;s ability to use its pre-change net operating loss, or NOL, carryforwards to offset its post-change taxable income may be limited. Limitations may also apply to the utilization of other pre-change tax attributes as a result of an ownership change. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Following the equity investment by Nestle Health Science in November 2016, we performed a Section&#160;382 analysis and determined that we experienced multiple ownership changes under Section&#160;382 of the Code prior to July 31, 2017. Utilization of the NOL and tax credit carryforwards are subject to a substantial annual limitation due to the ownership change limitations set forth in Internal Revenue Code Section&#160;382 and similar state provisions. Such annual limitations could impact the utilization of NOL and tax credit carryforwards in the future. We experienced no significant permanent losses of tax attributes due to these ownership changes.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition, we may experience more ownership changes under Section 382 of the Code as a result of future changes in our stock ownership, some of which may be outside our control. As a result, our ability to utilize NOL carryforwards or other tax attributes, such as research tax credits, in any taxable year may be further limited if we have experienced an ownership change.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Tax benefits from uncertain tax positions are recognized when it is more likely than not that the position will be sustained upon examination, including resolutions of any related appeals or litigation processes, based on technical merits. The amount recognized is measured as the largest amount of tax benefit that is greater than 50% likely of being realized upon effective settlement.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000313" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfUnrecognizedTaxBenefitsRollForwardTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001631650_20190101_20191231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">10. Defined Contribution Plan</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We sponsor a 401(k) Plan, or the 401(k) Plan, which stipulates that eligible employees may contribute to the 401(k) Plan subject to certain limitations. We may match employee contributions in amounts to be determined at our sole discretion. Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">None.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="ITEM_9A_CONTROLS_PROCEDURES">Item 9A. Controls and Procedures.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As required by Rule 13a-15(b) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, or the Exchange Act, our management, under the supervision and with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, has evaluated the effectiveness of the design and operation of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Exchange Act) as of December 31, 2019. Based on the evaluation of our disclosure controls and procedures, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer have concluded that, as of December 31, 2019, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective at the reasonable assurance level.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management&#8217;s Annual Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rule 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) of the Exchange Act). Internal control over financial reporting is a process designed by, or under the supervision of, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, and effected by our Board of Directors, management and other personnel, to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles and includes those policies and procedures that: </p>

<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</span></p></td>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, we conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2019 based on the criteria established in Internal Control - Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission, or COSO 2013. Based on our evaluation under the criteria set forth in Internal Control - Integrated Framework issued by the COSO, our management concluded our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 31, 2019.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2019 has been audited by KPMG LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, as stated in its attestation report included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were no changes in our internal control over financial reporting during the quarter ended December 31, 2019 identified in connection with the evaluation required by Rule&#160;13a-15(d)&#160;and 15d-15(d)&#160;of the Exchange Act that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Inherent Limitations on Effectiveness of Controls</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect all errors and all fraud. A control system, no matter how well conceived and operated, can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance that the objectives of the control system are met. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness of internal control to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate. Accordingly, our disclosure controls and procedures are designed to provide reasonable, not absolute, assurance that the objectives of our disclosure control system are met.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="ITEM_9B_OR_INFORMATION">Item 9B. Other Information.</p>
